This sheet covers the written parts of Lab 3 (Mixed Integer Programming and Facility Siting in JuMP). Do the coding in `lab03.ipynb` or `lab03.jl`. If you do not hand in your sheet at the end of class, submit a scanned PDF to Gradescope by **9:00pm on Wednesday, November 11**; you don't need to submit your code. See `lab03.ipynb` or `lab03.pdf` for the full description of the county. Each part can be answered in a sentence or two.

A county's four towns collect organic matter (food scraps and yard waste) every week, and the county will compost all of it. It can build composting sites at three candidate locations, A, B and C. A site that is built has a fixed cost each week and can take up to its capacity, and hauling organic matter from a town to a site costs a set amount per ton.

| Town | Organic Matter (tons/week) | To Site A (\$/ton) | To Site B (\$/ton) | To Site C (\$/ton) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Town 1 | 60 | 5 | 17 | 22 |
| Town 2 | 140 | 4 | 10 | 18 |
| Town 3 | 80 | 12 | 6 | 22 |
| Town 4 | 100 | 22 | 20 | 6 |

| Site | Capacity (tons/week) | Fixed cost (\$/week) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| A | 300 | 2,800 |
| B | 200 | 2,200 |
| C | 250 | 2,600 |

Let $x_{ij} \geq 0$ be the organic matter hauled from town $i$ to site $j$ (tons/week), and $y_j$ be 1 if site $j$ is built and 0 if not. With $d_i$ the organic matter town $i$ collects, $K_j$ and $F_j$ the capacity and fixed cost of site $j$, and $c_{ij}$ the transport cost, the model is below. In step 1, we will assume that we build every site (every $y_j = 1$).

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}} \quad & \sum_{i} \sum_{j} c_{ij} x_{ij} + \sum_{j} F_j y_j \\
\text{subject to:} \quad & \sum_{j} x_{ij} = d_i \\
& \sum_{i} x_{ij} \leq K_j y_j \qquad \text{for each site } j \\
& x_{ij} \geq 0, \quad y_j \in \{0, 1\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

## Step 2: Let the Model Choose the Sites

Which site(s) are not built? Show that the weekly amount saved compared with Step 1 equals that site's fixed cost minus the additional cost of hauling its town's organic matter somewhere else.

## Step 3: A Watershed Rule

Sites A and C drain to the same creek, upstream of a drinking-water intake, and the state will permit at most one composting site in that creek's watershed.

**(a)** Write the rule as a constraint on $y_A$, $y_B$ and $y_C$.
\vspace{0.8in}

**(b)** What is now built? How much does the rule cost the county each week?
